description: This module creates and manages CloudWatch event rules and targets.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A description of the rule.

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: event_pattern
parameters.description: A string pattern that is used to match against incoming events to determine if the rule should be triggered.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the rule you are creating, updating or deleting. No spaces or special characters allowed (i.e. must match [\.\-_A-Za-z0-9]+).

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: role_arn
parameters.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role associated with the rule.

parameters.name: schedule_expression
parameters.description: A cron or rate expression that defines the schedule the rule will trigger on. For example, cron(0 20 * * ? *), rate(5 minutes).

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Whether the rule is present (and enabled), disabled, or absent. Choices: "present" ← (default) "disabled" "absent"

parameters.name: targets
parameters.description: A list of targets to add to or update for the rule. Default: []

parameters.name: arn
parameters.description: The ARN associated with the target.

parameters.name: ecs_parameters
parameters.description: Contains the ECS task definition and task count to be used, if the event target is an ECS task.

parameters.name: task_count
parameters.description: The number of tasks to create based on task definition.

parameters.name: task_definition_arn
parameters.description: The full ARN of the task definition.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique target assignment ID.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: A JSON object that will override the event data passed to the target. If neither targets.input nor targets.input_path nor targets.input_transformer is specified, then the entire event is passed to the target in JSON form.

parameters.name: input_path
parameters.description: A JSONPath string (e.g. $.detail) that specifies the part of the event data to be passed to the target. If neither targets.input nor targets.input_path nor targets.input_transformer is specified, then the entire event is passed to the target in JSON form.

parameters.name: input_transformer
parameters.description: Settings to support providing custom input to a target based on certain event data.

parameters.name: input_paths_map
parameters.description: A dict that specifies the transformation of the event data to custom input parameters.

parameters.name: input_template
parameters.description: A string that templates the values input_paths_map extracted from the event data. It is used to produce the output you want to be sent to the target.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
- amazon.aws.cloudwatchevent_rule:
    name: MyCronTask
    schedule_expression: "cron(0 20 * * ? *)"
    description: Run my scheduled task
    targets:
      - id: MyTargetId
        arn: arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:MyFunction

- amazon.aws.cloudwatchevent_rule:
    name: MyDisabledCronTask
    schedule_expression: "rate(5 minutes)"
    description: Run my disabled scheduled task
    state: disabled
    targets:
      - id: MyOtherTargetId
        arn: arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:MyFunction
        input: '{"foo": "bar"}'

- amazon.aws.cloudwatchevent_rule:
    name: MyInstanceLaunchEvent
    description: "Rule for EC2 instance launch"
    state: present
    event_pattern: '{"source":["aws.ec2"],"detail-type":["EC2 Instance State-change Notification"],"detail":{"state":["pending"]}}'
    targets:
      - id: MyTargetSnsTopic
        arn: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:MySNSTopic
        input_transformer:
          input_paths_map:
            instance: "$.detail.instance-id"
            state: "$.detail.state"
          input_template: "<instance> is in state <state>"

- amazon.aws.cloudwatchevent_rule:
    name: MyCronTask
    state: absent

return_values.name: rule
return_values.description: CloudWatch Event rule data. Returned: success

return_values.name: arn
return_values.description: The ARN associated with the rule. Returned: success Sample: "arn:aws:events:us-east-1:123456789012:rule/MyCronTask"

return_values.name: description
return_values.description: A description of the rule. Returned: success Sample: "Run my scheduled task"

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: The name of the rule you are creating, updating or deleting. Returned: success Sample: "MyCronTask"

return_values.name: schedule_expression
return_values.description: A cron or rate expression that defines the schedule the rule will trigger on. Returned: success Sample: "cron(0 20 * * ? *)"

return_values.name: state
return_values.description: Whether the rule is present (and enabled), disabled, or absent. Returned: success Sample: "enabled"

return_values.name: targets
return_values.description: CloudWatch Event target(s) assigned to the rule. Returned: success

return_values.name: id
return_values.description: The unique target assignment ID. Returned: success Sample: "MyTargetId"
